scenes.narration: The first reaction is not adaptation. It is panic. Cold water triggers a gasp reflex you cannot consciously override.
That gasp can pull water into your lungs, which is why open water is dangerous even for strong swimmers.
Within seconds your blood vessels clamp shut and blood pressure jumps sharply. This is why cold exposure is risky for untrained hearts.
Then adrenaline and norepinephrine surge, sometimes several times their baseline, and that is the alertness people report afterwards.
Regular exposure appears to raise baseline norepinephrine and improve mood, though most studies remain small.
Start with cold water at the end of a normal shower. The controlled dose is where the benefit lives.
